items.title: Anthropic files for a blockbuster IPO
items.oneliner: Anthropic disclosed $17 billion revenue and 11,900 customers. Frontier model economics are now public-market scale.

items.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Hydrogen
items.oneliner: Google's coding model pairs with Orchestrator for dynamic routing. Multi-model stacks are becoming the default engineering pattern.

items.title: Small devices are getting usable LLMs
items.oneliner: Smolmaxxing shows old phones and TV boxes can run LLMs. Edge inference is moving from demo to optimization race.

items.title: An ancient PostgreSQL bug reached RCE
items.oneliner: A 22-year-old PostgreSQL type confusion bug became remote code execution. Managed database trust just took a hit.

items.title: Samsung TV ads were trivially hijacked
items.oneliner: A Samsung TV owner intercepted Smart Hub ad traffic and replaced ads with family photos. Consumer device trust remains flimsy.

items.title: Google paid seven figures for Chrome
items.oneliner: Google paid $1,333,337 for a Chrome logic bug. Browser exploit chains still command elite software bounties.

items.title: AWS Lambda idle billing gets exposed
items.oneliner: Easel says Lambda Web Functions bill memory for seven idle minutes. Serverless economics still hide expensive footguns.

items.title: Rust gets a JIT for iteration
items.oneliner: Relax compiles Rust functions on demand instead of waiting for full builds. Faster edit-run loops could reshape Rust workflows.

items.title: Rust 1.100 lands with type cleanup
items.oneliner: Rust 1.100 stabilizes the never type and updates Cargo internals. Mature languages still win by sanding sharp edges.

items.title: Linux bends around giant GPU BARs
items.oneliner: One Linux setup fit four 32 GB Resizable BARs behind a PCIe switch. Multi-GPU plumbing is still painfully bespoke.
